subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 encode opposite cron lifecycle contracts, and the choice affects existing persisted jobs, future session retention, and user-visible upgrade behavior.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a path for already-persisted omitted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only rejection
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation direction after callers, recovery, and docs are reconciled.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the default only for new jobs while explicitly documenting that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a path for already-persisted omitted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron defaulting, store compatibility, and product lifecycle semantics in files with recent steipete history.
